title: Allowed IP ranges: an IPv6 CIDR entry never matches at the sign-in gate or the save check (matcher reads IPv4 CIDR and exact addresses only), while the setting promises CIDR ranges
body:
domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6Cbvcmv8YWFhFJwzjKL

Filing gate: ② found by the contract review of PR #30309 (card #30203, record 6650936040), outside that card's door. **Read, not measured** — the first act is to measure it. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade.
Reader: `domain:server`, `plugin-auth` (`auth-manager.ts` `ipMatchesRange`, `isClientIpAllowed`), the `allowed_ip_ranges` help text in `service-settings` `auth.manifest.ts`.
Dedupe: `ipv6 cidr` → none open. **New.**

## What the reading says

`ipMatchesRange` matches an IPv4 CIDR and an exact address (IPv4-mapped addresses folded). An IPv6 CIDR entry such as `2001:db8::/32` falls back to exact match and so never matches a real client. The setting's help text promises "CIDR ranges" unqualified. Effect: an admin who allows an IPv6 range locks out every IPv6 client in it at the sign-in gate; after PR #30309 the save check refuses that save for an IPv6 admin (fail-safe), with copy that says the list does not include an address it textually covers.

## Wanted

- [ ] Measure: an IPv6 client inside an allowed IPv6 CIDR, at the gate and at the save.
- [ ] Either match IPv6 CIDR in `ipMatchesRange` (both doors share it), or refuse an IPv6 CIDR entry at save with a clear message and say "IPv4 CIDR" in the help text.
- [ ] Pin both families.

Links: #30203, PR #30309.
